title: flw contract
description: specs/current.toml — one per project, complete and current. It states what is true when the work is done, never how to get there: how each version came about lives in one file per version under specs/versions/. Five questions, one home each — what exists (final_state.components), what a user can do with it (provides), what is gone (final_state.removed), how we know it works (success_criteria), and what would force a redesign if false (assumptions).

schema_version.description: Selects the schema. validate_spec.py dispatches on this rather than on the path it was given.

spec_version.description: LINE.MAJOR.MINOR. The line is 0 until a record declares release_line, and 1 once it has, marking the point the product moved from not-real to real; the major and minor fold behind it, moving by each applied record's classification suffix — major when a behaviour someone relied on now works differently, minor when a capability arrives and nothing that worked before changed. Scoped to this one contract: a repository whose parts release independently is several contracts, one per part at the root nearest_project resolves each to, never a single number folded across all of them.

components.description: What exists when the work is done. A component may be conceptual rather than file-shaped — one capability spanning several files is one component.

removed.description: What this contract has deleted. Stating a removal is not the op that performs it, so a set here never forces a major bump on its own.

tests.description: Commands that must exit 0. These are the project's own — flw bakes in no test runner, no linter and no toolchain. `flw test -A` runs them and reports; it does not judge whether the work is done.

criteria.description: What the tests cannot express. Required even when tests are present: a suite that passes is not the same claim as the work being done, and pretending otherwise is how a green build ships the wrong thing.

assumptions.description: What would force a redesign if it turned out false. Required, and an empty list is a legitimate answer — the point is that the question was asked, not that it produced entries. Phrase as testable propositions ('input fits in memory'), not intents ('data is small').

open_questions.description: Raised and not settled. Optional, because a contract with none is a complete contract. Better here than answered by assumption.

applied.description: The names of the version records whose runs have finished, oldest first. This is where the order of versions lives: flw-execute appends to it in the step that applies a version's contract_edit, so the order is written once, where the work landed, rather than inferred from a chain only one branch can hold.

name.description: The natural key. Amendments address a component by name, so changing it is a remove plus an add — which is why rename needs no op of its own, and why names must be unique (checked semantically; the schema language has no uniqueItems here).

paths.description: Where this component lives, project-relative. Directories end in '/'. Nothing materializes these — they locate the component for a reader and for review.

provides.description: What a user can do, one capability per entry. This is the product surface. A component that provides nothing is a file list, not a component.

implementation.description: Optional. How this component is built — the mechanism, not the guarantee. 'SQLite, one file per user, no ORM' qualifies; 'probably use a dataclass' does not. Distinguish the three fields by what the sentence is about, not by whether a test could reach it: `provides` is about what a user can do, `properties` is about what the component guarantees, `implementation` is about how it is built — a mechanism value like a damping constant is perfectly testable and still belongs here. If it does not constrain, it is not spec, and it belongs in the version file's approach or nowhere.

properties.description: Optional. Falsifiable statements about what the component guarantees — an invariant a test can be written against. A sentence that cannot be false does not belong here, and neither does a restatement of a `provides` entry: a capability and an invariant read alike, but one is about a person and the other is about a function.

surfaces.description: Optional. Things that break someone outside this project when they change: subcommands and flags, exit codes, state files and their keys, config keys, tagged-block markers, install locations. A private helper is not one, however visible.

statement.description: What is gone, in the author's words.

check.description: A command that exits non-zero while the removed thing is still present. Optional on purpose — some removals are conceptual, and a fabricated check is worse than an honest absence.

command.description: Run from the project root; must exit 0. No runner allow-list — v2 had one because it carried a language registry, and the registry is gone.
